newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence minister says backs arms treaty.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister says backs arms treaty.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Wednesday that Russia's parliament should ratify the START-2 nuclear arms reduction treaty and he lashed out at those opposing his attempts to reform the struggling armed forces.
"I not only favour it (START-2), I favour the next treaty, START-3, to continue arms reduction," Rodionov told reporters after more than two hours of talks with U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry.

Perry, who began a visit to Russia on Wednesday, will speak to the State Duma lower house of parliament on Thursday to try to persuade deputies to ratify START-2, which would cut stategic nuclear warheads to a third of Cold War levels on both sides.

A senior U.S. defence official told reporters that Perry had stressed to Rodionov that billions of dollars could be saved by reducing nuclear weapons and that those funds would help in the minister's drive to reform Russia's cash-strapped armed forces.

"We have a lot of talk about reform in the armed forces. We have a lot of criticism that nothing is being done," Rodionov said in response to a question about criticism of steps he plans to cut airborne forces.
"All say that reform is necessary, but 'not my service, don't touch my service'," said Rodionov.
